title: Scripture and Preaching
definition: Scripture and Preaching means the public proclamation of God’s Word so people may hear truth, behold Christ, repent, believe, and grow.
summary: Scripture and Preaching means the public proclamation of God’s Word so people may hear truth, behold Christ, repent, believe, and grow.
christFocus: Jesus preached the kingdom of God, fulfilled the Scriptures, and sends His servants to proclaim His Word faithfully.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Preaching is not motivational speaking with Bible verses added. It is the faithful proclamation of God’s Word. The preacher stands under Scripture, not above it, and must make the meaning clear.

Biblical preaching points people to Christ, exposes sin, proclaims grace, calls for faith, strengthens believers, and equips the Church. It should serve the hearers, not the ego of the speaker.

The power of preaching is not in personality, volume, or cleverness. The Holy Spirit works through the Word to awaken faith, convict hearts, comfort the afflicted, and build up Christ’s people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have heard preaching that entertained, pressured, shamed, or centered the preacher. Scripture and preaching reminds the Church that preaching belongs to God and must serve Christ’s sheep.

This doctrine also encourages small faithful ministries. A sermon does not need fame to be fruitful; it needs Scripture, Christ, love, and dependence on the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: If you preach or teach, handle God’s Word faithfully and point people to Christ. If you hear preaching, listen with discernment and humility, asking the Holy Spirit to help you receive truth and obey what Scripture teaches.
